transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-05
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Evan (Redwood SE), Liam (Brightwater), Priya (Brightwater), Sam (Brightwater), Rosa (Brightwater Security)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff to align on launchpad plan. Main asks: VPC options, compliance docs, and a short bench to validate latency & cost.

00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you say your name and role?
00:12 Liam (Brightwater): Liam Carter, Head of ML at Brightwater. Hey, thanks for organizing.
00:16 Priya (Brightwater): Priya Nair, infra lead — I'm here for networking and the VPC bits.
00:20 Sam (Brightwater): Sam Ortiz, PM for customer-facing features.
00:23 Rosa (Brightwater): Rosa Chen, security. I'll be checking compliance and KMS needs.
00:27 Jordan: Great. From our side Maya is CSM, Evan SE — we'll kick off the onboarding runbook.
00:33 Maya (CSM): Hi all, excited to sync. We'll aiming for a fast pilot but want to make sure we cover the security runway.
00:41 Evan (SE): I'll be leading the perf and integration checks — we'll map out a small benchmark plan today.
00:50 Jordan: Cool. First up, timeline. We're thinking two-week rapid trial to validate latency and integration, then decide hosted vs dedicated after bench results. Is that in line with you?
01:05 Liam: Sounds good. Our main success metrics are p95 latency under 350ms on short prompts and cost per 1k tokens under a threshold. Also model quality stability across 1k prompts.
01:22 Evan: Okay, on the p95, quick note — that depends a lot on sequence length and batching. We'll ask for representative token distros.
01:35 Priya: For networking, what's the VPC pattern? We prefer a customer-VPC peering or private link.
01:43 Jordan: Redwood supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-style connections for Private deployments. For Hosted we can offer tokenized ingress with IP allowlist, but for Dedicated/Private we can do direct peering.
01:58 Priya: Right, if we go dedicated we need to confirm ingress CIDRs and whether we can bring our own KMS.
02:07 Rosa: And from security, we'll need SOC2 type II, encryption-at-rest details, and audit log retention. Also the SAML SSO flow and RBAC controls.
02:20 Maya: We'll share the security pack — it includes our SOC2 summary, encryption docs, and SSO guide.
02:28 Rosa: Perfect, please include any HSM/KMS integration notes. We may need to route keys through our KMS.
02:37 Evan: Technical aside — if you bring your own KMS on a Private deployment, there are extra handshake steps but it's supported. We also support envelope encryption workflows and audit hooks.
02:51 Sam: For the bench, can we scope a small sweep: 5k short prompts across 3 models to see latency and token cost?
02:59 Evan: Yep, that's a good starter. We'll run a 5k-message latency/cost sweep. We'll also test prefix caching scenarios to measure throughput improvements.
03:13 Liam: On models — we use a mix of open LLMs and some tuned variants. We might want to test both a quantized 8-bit variant and a FP16 hosted model. How does Redwood handle quantization?
03:27 Evan: The runtime supports quantized variants and switches kernels based on the model flavor — but perf will differ. We'll include both in the sweep. Note that memory and latency tradeoffs will show up in results.
03:40 Jordan: Competitors might do similar — you mentioned you talked to Vertex and a self-hosted option?
03:45 Liam: Yeah we did a quick talk with Vertex and our own infra team about self-hosting; key concerns are control and cost. We want to compare unit economics.
03:55 Maya: We can provide a cost breakdown post-bench. Also if you need reserved capacity options, Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput.
04:08 Priya: For Dedicated, what's the autoscaling and burst behavior? We have traffic spikes; we need graceful degradation without throwing errors to users.
04:18 Evan: Dedicated pools have configurable autoscale and burst buckets. There's a fallback policy: if capacity is reached, requests can route to a compatible hosted variant automatically. We'll show the routing demo in the tech run.
04:33 Rosa: Can you also confirm logging retention and where logs are stored? We need audit logs for 1 year and an API to pull them.
04:41 Maya: Yes, audit logs are available and retention can be configured as an add-on. We'll include that detail in the security pack.
04:50 Sam: On the integration side, our app will call Redwood via the REST SDK; we want streaming for the chat UI. Any caveats?
04:58 Evan: Streaming is supported. For low-latency streaming we recommend websocket streaming or chunked responses; we'll share best-practice config for the SDK and typical buffer sizes.
05:12 Liam: One little thing — our prompt patterns include long context windows 1-2k tokens with short replies. That changes batching behavior, right?
05:22 Evan: Yes, long contexts will impact KV cache usage and memory — we'll capture that in the perf run. Also we'll look at continuous batching vs per-request latency tradeoffs.
05:33 Jordan: Great. Logistics: Evan will own the bench run, Maya will own scheduling and the runbook, Liam/Priya provide samples and infra access, Rosa will review security docs.
05:47 Sam: Expected decision point? We hope to decide hosted trial vs dedicated eval within two weeks after the bench.
05:55 Jordan: Sounds doable. Any blockers?
06:00 Rosa: No blockers if we get SOC2 and KMS notes. Also need to confirm data residency — our EU clients' data must remain in EU region.
06:11 Maya: We'll call out region options and deploy to EU region for the bench.
06:18 Evan: One more note — if you want on-prem/private deployment later there are extra infra requirements; we'll include the checklist.
06:26 Priya: We'll review the checklist but prefer hosted trial first to validate.
06:31 Jordan: Okay wrapping up — recap and next steps.
06:35 Jordan: Evan to run 5k-message latency & cost sweep (deadline 2026-06-12).
06:40 Maya: I'll share onboarding runbook + security pack by 2026-06-07.
06:45 Liam: We'll send sample prompts and traffic shape by 2026-06-08.
06:50 Rosa: I'll send security contact and confirm KMS requirements by 2026-06-09.
06:56 Jordan: We'll schedule a follow-up bench walk-through with your infra team — propose 2026-06-13 or 14.
07:05 Sam: 13th works for us.
07:08 Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll capture action items in the shared doc and follow up in email.
07:15 Meeting end.
